### Module 02 — Descriptive Statistics for Clinical Variables

# Descriptive Statistics for Clinical Variables

***
**Learning objectives**
- Compute prevalence, incidence, and rates with correct denominators
- Build stratified summaries by age group, sex, and payer
- Detect and handle right-skewed clinical distributions (LOS, charges)
- Apply age-standardisation (direct method) to remove age confounding
- Produce a publication-ready Table 1 with confidence intervals

**Estimated time:** 1.5 hours | **Level:** Beginner → Intermediate | **Libraries:** `dplyr` / tibble, `stats`

## 1. Setup & Dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

skewness <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  if (n < 3 || s == 0) return(NA_real_)
  mean((x - m)^3) / (s^3)
}

# ── Reconstruct shared dataset ───────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 800
ages      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes     <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers    <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                    N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days   <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges    <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
charges[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_
primary_dx <- sample(c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
                     N, replace = TRUE)
admit_type <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
                     N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02))
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  drg_code      = drg_codes,
  drg_label     = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx    = primary_dx,
  admit_type    = admit_type,
  los_days      = los_days,
  total_charge  = charges,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  ckd           = rbinom(N, 1, 0.15),
  heart_failure = rbinom(N, 1, 0.18),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14)
)
df$age_group <- cut(df$age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))
cat(sprintf("Dataset ready: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
```

## 2. Prevalence, Incidence & Rates


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── 2.1  Comorbidity prevalence ──────────────────────────────────────────────
comorbidities <- c("diabetes", "hypertension", "ckd", "heart_failure")

wilson_ci <- function(k, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  z   <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  p   <- k / n
  den <- 1 + z^2 / n
  mid <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / den
  hw  <- (z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))) / den
  c(round((mid - hw) * 100, 1), round((mid + hw) * 100, 1))
}

prev_df <- map_dfr(comorbidities, function(cond) {
  k <- sum(df[[cond]])
  n <- nrow(df)
  ci <- wilson_ci(k, n)
  tibble(
    Condition        = cond,
    `N cases`        = k,
    `Prevalence (%)` = round(k / n * 100, 1),
    `95% CI`         = sprintf("%s%%–%s%%", ci[1], ci[2])
  )
})
cat("Comorbidity prevalence (Wilson 95% CI):\n")
```

## 3. Skewed Distributions — LOS and Charges


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
for (pair in list(c("LOS (days)", "los_days"), c("Total charge ($)", "total_charge"))) {
  name <- pair[[1]]
  col  <- pair[[2]]
  s    <- df[[col]][!is.na(df[[col]])]
  sk   <- skewness(s)
  cat(name, "\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Mean    : %.2f   Median: %.2f   Diff: %.2f\n",
              mean(s), median(s), mean(s) - median(s)))
  cat(sprintf("  Std     : %.2f\n", sd(s)))
  cat(sprintf("  Skewness: %.3f  %s\n", sk,
              if (sk > 0.5) "→ right-skewed; use MEDIAN" else "→ approximately symmetric"))
  cat(sprintf("  P10–P90 : %.1f – %.1f\n\n",
              quantile(s, 0.10), quantile(s, 0.90)))
}
```

## 4. Age-Standardisation — Direct Method


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# US 2000 standard population weights by age group
std_pop <- tibble(
  age_group  = factor(c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"),
                      levels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+")),
  std_weight = c(0.3761, 0.3399, 0.1267, 0.0573)
)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
for (pyr in c("Medicare", "Private", "Medicaid")) {
  sub   <- df %>% filter(payer == pyr)
  crude <- mean(sub$readmitted_30) * 100
  rates <- sub %>%
    group_by(age_group) %>%
    summarise(crude_rate = mean(readmitted_30), .groups = "drop")
  m     <- rates %>% inner_join(std_pop, by = "age_group") %>%
    mutate(weighted = crude_rate * std_weight)
  adj   <- sum(m$weighted) * 100
  cat(sprintf("%-12s  %11.1f%%  %11.1f%%  %+7.1f%%\n", pyr, crude, adj, adj - crude))
}
```

## 5. Publication-Ready Table 1


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
table1 <- function(df, stratify, continuous, categorical) {
  groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(df[[stratify]])))
  records <- list()

  for (col in continuous) {
    sk <- abs(skewness(df[[col]]))
    use_median <- !is.na(sk) && sk > 1
    stat_label <- if (use_median) "median [IQR]" else "mean ± SD"
    row <- list(Variable = sprintf("%s (%s)", col, stat_label))
    for (g in groups) {
      vals <- df[[col]][df[[stratify]] == g]
      vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
      key  <- paste0(stratify, "=", g)
      if (use_median) {
        row[[key]] <- sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]",
                              median(vals), quantile(vals, 0.25), quantile(vals, 0.75))
      } else {
        row[[key]] <- sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f", mean(vals), sd(vals))
      }
    }
    records <- append(records, list(row))
  }

  for (col in categorical) {
    records <- append(records, list(list(Variable = col)))
    cats <- sort(unique(na.omit(df[[col]])))
    for (cat in cats) {
      row <- list(Variable = paste0("  ", as.character(cat)))
      for (g in groups) {
        sub <- df[df[[stratify]] == g, ]
        n   <- sum(sub[[col]] == cat, na.rm = TRUE)
        pct <- n / nrow(sub) * 100
        row[[paste0(stratify, "=", g)]] <- sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, pct)
      }
      records <- append(records, list(row))
    }
  }

  bind_rows(lapply(records, as_tibble))
}

t1 <- table1(
  df,
  stratify    = "readmitted_30",
  continuous  = c("age", "los_days", "total_charge"),
  categorical = c("sex", "payer", "admit_type", "age_group")
)
cat("Table 1 — Baseline characteristics by 30-day readmission status:\n")
```

## 6. Statistical Tests for Group Differences


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cat("Statistical tests: readmitted vs not readmitted\n\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Statistical tests: readmitted vs not readmitted
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Mann-Whitney U — skewed continuous
for (pair in list(c("los_days", "LOS"), c("age", "Age"))) {
  col   <- pair[[1]]
  label <- pair[[2]]
  g0 <- df[[col]][df$readmitted_30 == 0]
  g1 <- df[[col]][df$readmitted_30 == 1]
  g0 <- g0[!is.na(g0)]
  g1 <- g1[!is.na(g1)]
  sk <- skewness(df[[col]])
  if (abs(sk) > 0.5) {
    wt <- wilcox.test(g0, g1, alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("%s (skewed → Mann-Whitney U): U=%.0f, p=%.4f\n",
                label, wt$statistic, wt$p.value))
  } else {
    tt <- t.test(g0, g1)
    cat(sprintf("%s (normal → t-test): t=%.3f, p=%.4f\n",
                label, unname(tt$statistic), tt$p.value))
  }
}
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# Chi-square — categorical
for (col in c("sex", "payer", "admit_type")) {
  ct  <- table(df[[col]], df$readmitted_30)
  chi <- chisq.test(ct)
  sig <- if (chi$p.value < 0.05) "*" else ""
  cat(sprintf("%-12s (chi-square): χ²=%.2f, df=%d, p=%.4f %s\n",
              col, unname(chi$statistic), unname(chi$parameter), chi$p.value, sig))
}
```

## 7. Knowledge Check
1. Why is the Wilson interval preferred over the normal-approximation CI for proportions near 0 or 1?
2. After age-standardisation, Private insurance shows a *higher* readmission rate than crude. What does this mean?

4. What does a significant chi-square for `payer × readmission` imply for the analysis plan?
